title: The six non-venture sub-prompts never mention the 2026-11-24 North star, so their runs pick targets with no for-profit hint
problem: prompt.md and CLAUDE.md say for-profit products come first, but the weighted draw still sends ~37% of runs to explore, perf, polish, creative, quality and redteam, and none of their prompt-0.md files said anything about the North star or where the for-profit products are listed. Runs on those tracks reported having to decide for themselves (or not) whether to aim at paid products, and one perf run guessed which pages feed a paid bet.
evidence: prompts/runs/2026-11-24/25 *.json: 57 runs on the six tracks; 4 name the gap in doc_friction (polish 01AcxTtLCaLcFtYBebsPEYK3, explore 01EhTJVMqoW3GBnC2yy1TVXe, creative 01XpHqycpy3auKHtGfeZpbAt, perf 01EhTJVMQnbSD8Erfmd51Ydz); perf 01E5sJKkQYjyBhXkJPTK7Eas: 'no row names a bet's core paid product'
grep -n -i 'north star|for-profit' prompts/{explore,perf,polish,creative,quality,redteam}/prompt-0.md on main 2026-11-25: no hits
change: One paragraph in each of the six prompt-0.md files: where the track leaves the target open, prefer one that serves a for-profit product, and `python3 portfolio/monetization/transition.py` lists them. No routing weight change (the draw is the owner's split; a reweight would be a review-track or owner call).
metric: share of runs on these six tracks whose doc_friction names a missing North star / for-profit hint; secondarily, share whose PR touches a transition.json proprietary venture
source: process critique, 2026-11-25 (doc friction of recent runs)
